checks.label: Because we have sinusoidal variation in time, the vertical component (magnitude times the sine of the angle it makes with the x axis) gives v(t): at every moment of the first screen's turn, and at every arm length on the third, the pen sits level with the arm's tip at the arm's length times the sine of its angle, and every drawn point of the wave is that height at its time

The length of the second hand represents the height or amplitude of the sine wave: at every arm length from 1 to 10 the arm is drawn that long on the circle, the wave over one turn reaches exactly that height and sinks to minus it, and the label on its peak reads amplitude and that length

The frequency indicates how many cycles exist in one second: on a graph always one second wide, at every setting from 1 to 10 turns a second each drawn wave is one turn of the arm, so exactly that many waves fill the second, the axis marks 0.5 s and 1 s at every setting, and the period bracket over the first wave reads 1 ÷ f
Low voltage supplies shall be 50 hertz: the row under the one-second graph works out a UK supply's period, 1 ÷ 50 = 0.02 s = 20 ms
360° = 2π radians: one turn is marked 2π, so f turns a second is 2πf radians a second, and the ω pill reads 2π × 50 = 314.16 rad/s at 50 Hz and 2π times the turns a second at every other setting

A(t) = Amax sin(ωt) = Amax sin(2πft): at 50 Hz every drawn point of the wave, read off the graph at its time t in seconds, equals sin(2π × 50 × t), and the arm points right again at the end of each turn, 20 ms and 40 ms

The terminal side of the angle intersects the circle at the point (x, y), which is equivalent to (cos t, sin t): at every start angle and time, arm B's tip is drawn at (cos θ, sin θ) times its length, its pen draws the sine, the switch traces arm A's across shadow, the cosine, and at a start angle of 90° that trace lies exactly on wave B

A start angle φ slides the whole wave left by φ ÷ ω, and a negative one slides it right: at every start angle from −180° to 180°, wave B at each drawn time is wave A a time φ ÷ ω later, the bracket between their peaks reads that slide, left or right, and at 90° it is a quarter period left, 5 ms at 50 Hz

A level line between the peaks meets each wave twice: at every height from −10 to 10 each dot lies on the drawn wave and the line; at 5 the first two are at 1.67 ms and 8.33 ms (0.524 and 2.618 radians ÷ 314.16), and the wave first reaches −8.3 at 13.1 ms (π + 0.979 = 4.121 radians), with 16.9 ms next

tan 135° = sin 135° ÷ cos 135° = 0.707 ÷ −0.707 = −1: once answered, the graph carries on past the gap at 90° and its pen sits at −1 at 135°, every drawn point of that piece is sin θ ÷ cos θ, and before the answer only the piece up to 90° is drawn

The slope tan θ = sin θ ÷ cos θ: the trace is sin θ ÷ cos θ at every drawn angle, cut off at 4 and −4; it is 0 at 0° and 1 at 45°, has no value at 90° and 270°, where the across shadow is 0, and repeats every half turn

Every worked number matches the lesson: sin 180° = 0 with slips −1 and 1; 4 × sin 30° = 2 with slips 3.46 and 0.5; 1 ÷ 0.01 = 100 Hz with slips 0.01 and 10; 1 ÷ 50 = 0.02 s, 20 ms; ω = 2π × 50 = 314.16; π = 3.14159; 100π ÷ 2π = 50 Hz with slips 314.2 and 100; π/2 = 1.571 and 5 ms; 0.5, 0.524, 2.618, 1.67 ms and 8.33 ms; −0.979, 4.121, 13.1 ms with slips 3.1 ms (0.979 ÷ 314.16) and 16.9 ms (5.304, the second crossing); tan 45° = 1; tan 135° = 0.707 ÷ −0.707 = −1; 325 sin(314.2t) with slips 50t and 100t, and 7.96; 20 sin(π/2) = 20 with slips 0 and 1

Each puzzle accepts only its right answer, every wrong answer has its own hint and its own red row of working, the answer appears once it is given, and before an answer nothing in the picture gives it away

No label sits on another label or a handle, or runs off the picture, on any screen in any state: puzzles answered right, wrong or with Why? open, the arm dragged to every time, every arm length, turns a second, start angle and switch setting, and the level line at every height
Every demonstration has finished within 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; each answer and Why? has settled within 1.8 s
